name: Milo's Tea Company, Inc.
old_description: Milo’s teas, lemonades, and fruit punch are made with high-quality ingredients and no preservatives for a delicious, homemade taste.
about:
Milo's Tea Company, Inc. operates from Bessemer, Alabama. For more than 80 years, the company has followed the philosophy of its founders, Milo and Bea Carlton, who believed in doing things the right way and never sacrificing taste. The business remains family-made, adhering to the original approach of using high-quality ingredients without preservatives.

The company produces a line of iced teas, lemonades, and fruit punches, all formulated to be 100% natural. Seasonal offerings such as Peach Sweet Tea join the core lineup. Production details such as facility size, headcount, or annual volume are not publicly disclosed.

Milo's beverages are sold through retail channels where consumers can locate products via a store finder. The brand also engages directly with fans through a dedicated community page and an online merchandise store offering apparel and drinkware.

The company's stated differentiation rests on a commitment to "no short cuts, no nonsense" — using only high-quality ingredients, avoiding preservatives, and maintaining a family-made process that aims to deliver a homemade taste.

name: Miltronics Manufacturing, Inc.
old_description: Pacer Instruments™ specializes in high quality test and measurement equipment, providing high quality instruments that exceed the industry standards for accuracy, reliability, and ease of operation.
about:
Miltronics Manufacturing, Inc., based in Keene, New Hampshire, has been operating for more than three decades. The company, also known as Miltronics Manufacturing Services, Inc., does not publicly disclose its founding year, ownership structure, or founders' names. It began with a focus on high-reliability electronics, leveraging a strict military electronics background to build a reputation for dependability.

The firm provides electronics manufacturing services and subcontract manufacturing to a range of industries. In addition to contract work, Miltronics designs and produces its own branded product lines, including the Driveway Alert® wireless detection systems, Forklift Alert™ proximity warning systems, Freedom Fence® pet containment systems, and Pacer Instruments™ precision test and measurement equipment. The company emphasizes a flexible working environment that supports a variety of assembly techniques, prototyping, design-for-manufacture, and full build-and-test capabilities, all performed with what it describes as state-of-the-art manufacturing equipment.

Miltronics serves customers in military electronics and other sectors requiring high-reliability electronic assemblies. Its subcontracting services are positioned for companies seeking a long-term partner for prototype development, first-article production, ongoing part supply, and inventory-stocking programs. The company does not list specific industry verticals beyond its military heritage and general electronics manufacturing.

Miltronics cites its dependability, cost-effectiveness, and quick response to changing customer requirements as key differentiators. All systems are manufactured in the USA, and the company highlights its evolution from a first-article supplier to a partner that can stock parts and build and test on demand.

name: MinnTech Plastics
old_description: Stock products and Custom thermoformed trays, clamshells, and containers in APET, RPET & CPET. Food safe, recyclable, and engineered for performance.
about:
MinnTech Plastics operates from Rogers, Minnesota, where it runs a modern manufacturing facility producing thermoformed trays, clamshells, and containers. The company does not publicly state its founding year or ownership details.

The company specializes in custom thermoformed packaging using APET, RPET, and CPET materials. Its in-house capabilities include CNC trim tooling, custom mold design, rapid prototyping, and production-grade aluminum tooling. The facility supports scalable runs from small sample orders to full production volumes, with multi-point quality inspection and optimized logistics.

MinnTech serves the food industry, airline catering, and specialty markets, counting national food brands among its customers. One reference comes from INCorporated Plastics, whose president Craig Gould describes MinnTech as a manufacturer partner for PET containers.

The company emphasizes precision engineering, food safety compliance, and sustainability. It highlights tight-tolerance thermoforming, FDA-compliant materials, 100% recyclable Category #1 plastics, and transparent pricing with no hidden fees. Its CPET trays withstand temperatures from -40°F to 375°F, enabling freezer-to-oven use.

about:
Minnesota Equipment is based in Rogers, Minnesota, where it operates as a licensed John Deere dealer providing new and used equipment, parts, and service for yard and farm work. The company’s founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The dealership carries a range of outdoor power equipment including mowers, compact tractors, utility tractors, hay equipment, utility vehicles, snowblowers, and handheld tools. It stocks parts for most brands and offers service and repair for the equipment it sells. Trade-in evaluations are available for customers looking to upgrade their machinery.

Minnesota Equipment serves residential customers, commercial landscaping crews, agricultural operators, and government agencies. Its marketing segments reference adventurers, weekend warriors, multi-taskers, groundbreakers, and harvest heroes, reflecting a focus on both hobbyist and professional users in grounds maintenance and farming.

The company emphasizes quick, reliable trade-in evaluations and a broad parts inventory as reasons customers choose it, though it does not publish a formal mission statement or founding narrative.

name: Mispillion River Brewing
old_description: Send us pics from the streets on Facebook (don't take pictures while driving though)
about:
Mispillion River Brewing opened in Milford, Delaware in the fall of 2013. The brewery was started by the self-described "Mispillion Crew" with a focus on using high-quality barley, hops, water, and yeast to produce craft beer for a broad audience, from novices to enthusiasts.

The company brews and packages its own beer on-site, offering 16-ounce pints and 5-ounce samples in its tasting room, along with 4-pack cans, 32-ounce crowlers, and growler refills for take-home sales. The facility also operates a tasting room with daily hours and hosts live entertainment and food trucks on its patio.

The brewery serves the local Milford community and craft beer drinkers throughout the region.

Founded on the premise that beer should be fun on every level, Mispillion River Brewing emphasizes its passion for beer and its motivation from the local community. The company aims to honor craft brewing traditions through ingredient quality and service.

name: Mission Foods
old_description: Check out our best air fryer recipes. Perfect for an easy, delicious meal.
about:
Mission Foods operates as a subsidiary of Gruma Corporation, a tortilla manufacturer founded in 1949 that now leads the global market. While Gruma's roots trace back to Mexico, Mission Foods serves as the company's primary U.S. brand, with corporate headquarters in Irving, Texas, and a significant facility in Colorado Springs, Colorado. The business began as part of Gruma's expansion into the American market, leveraging the parent company's decades of tortilla-making expertise.

The company manufactures a broad line of Mexican-style foods, including flour and corn tortillas, wraps, flatbreads such as naan and pita, tortilla chips (offered in organic, protein, and grain-free varieties), chicharrones, and salsa. Product development has expanded into better-for-you categories: low-carb, high-fiber, high-protein, organic, and gluten-free formulations. Mission Foods describes itself as the number-one tortilla brand in the United States, though specific plant square footage, headcount, and annual volume are not publicly disclosed.

Products reach consumers through retail grocery channels and foodservice distributors, supported by a store locator on the company website. The brand also engages home cooks directly through a large recipe library organized around meal occasions—quick meals, party dishes, vegetarian, air-fryer preparations, and holiday collections. Industries served include consumer packaged goods, retail grocery, and foodservice.

Mission Foods frames its purpose around exploration and shared meals: "Great food is a great motivator. It brings everyone to the table and inspires us to explore all kinds of delicious destinations." The company says it seeks the freshest ingredients and simple recipes to create wholesome products that enable better-for-you eating without abandoning traditional favorites like tacos and nachos.

name: Mission Plastics
old_description: Injection molding customized to your specs, your timeline, and your expectations.
about:
Mission Plastics, headquartered in Grandview, Missouri, has specialized in custom injection molding since 1968. The company is family-owned and operated and operates as part of the Peterson Manufacturing family of businesses, which provides additional vertically integrated capabilities such as metal stamping, PCB manufacturing, and wire harness assembly.

Mission Plastics runs two facilities—in Greater Kansas City and Southwest Arkansas—totaling 198,000 square feet, including a 50,000-square-foot on-site tool shop. Its 96 injection molding machines range from 35 to 610 tons, with five vertical and three two-shot presses. The shop offers insert molding, overmolding, automation, mold design, engineering, prototyping, and turnkey manufacturing, all under ISO 9001:2015 and UL certification.

The molder serves consumer products, industrial applications, lawn and garden, and lenses and optics. Long-term customers include Milbank (cited by buyer Sarah Brown), a global manufacturer (referenced by its director of design and engineering), and a Fortune 500 company (noted by engineering manager Michael Ranta).

Mission Plastics emphasizes its family-owned culture, with many master crafters exceeding 20 years of tenure, and its financially stable, debt-free structure. Sustainability initiatives include returnable packaging systems, scrap reduction, and recycling programs aimed at reducing landfill waste.
